acceptance: pr-arm waits instead of refusing when the only failed core check comes from a text-edit placeholder run and the full CI run is still running.
context: Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-22 `make pr-arm PR=4443 HEAD=5c57945da… WAIT=55` refused at once with: "no verify-fast-duration verdict is recorded for 5c57945da: the core job ended failure for 5c57945da and no verdict will arrive; rerun it with make pr-rerun PR=4443, then arm again" and "required check 'core' completed with conclusion 'failure'". The failed `core` was the `CI (text edit)` placeholder run 45034069456 (event pull_request, 6 s), while the full `CI` run 45036340993 for the same head was in progress; that full run later passed and the PR armed. `docs/agent/merge-authority.md` says a placeholder failure stays `waiting` while the full run is in progress, and for a later head pr-arm did report the other placeholders (`results-data`, `docs`, `tooling`) as waiting. The `core` duration-verdict path does not apply the same rule, so it ends a WAIT early and advises a needless `make pr-rerun`, on which agents may spend their one rerun.

## Change
Make the duration-verdict check and the required-check reading in `scripts/pr_landing.py` (and the arm gate it uses) classify a failed `core` from a `CI (text edit)` placeholder run as `waiting` while a full CI run for the head is queued or in progress, as for the other placeholder checks.

## Decision gates
- A failed `core` in a full CI run stays a refusal; only placeholder runs change.
- Do not relax any required check or the would-block duration rule.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a test with the recorded shape of this case (placeholder `core` failure plus an in-progress full run) yields `waiting`, failing before the fix; a test with a failed `core` in a completed full run still yields `refused` with the rerun advice; existing pr-arm tests pass.
Fail: either case misclassified.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
